label: Shell
title: Shell
subtitle: Executes terminal commands on your machine. This is the most powerful — and most sensitive — tool available to agents. It can run scripts, install packages, call command-line tools, perform git operations, and do anything your terminal can do.
whenToUse: Use when a task requires running a script, building software, executing tests, or calling a CLI tool. Keep this tool under Ask-level approval while you are learning how an agent behaves.

methods.name: Execute Command
methods.description: Runs a shell command and returns stdout, stderr, and the exit code. Supports configurable working directory, environment variables, and a timeout.

mediaCaption: An Execute Command approval card showing the full command string, working directory, and timeout before the user approves
tips: Set this tool to Ask-level approval. Shell commands can delete files, modify system settings, or make network calls.
Long-running commands will time out. For background processes, use & or nohup inside the command.
When an approval is required, the request shows the exact command (and working directory) in a formatted block so you can review precisely what will run before allowing it.
